# Pre-Implementation Checklist: TCGplayer Packing Slip Order Import

**Purpose**: Formal pre-implementation gate — a broad requirements-quality review of spec.md (and its plan.md/tasks.md follow-through) before authorizing `/speckit-implement` execution, per this project's constitution.
**Created**: 2026-08-20
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are field-format requirements defined for all four V1 target games (Pokémon, Magic, Lorcana, One Piece), or does the spec assume a single uniform description format validated only against Pokémon/Magic/Lorcana examples? [Gap, Spec §FR-002, Clarifications]
- [x] CHK002 Is behavior specified for a technically-readable PDF that contains zero order pages at all (distinct from FR-005's "an order with zero product lines" and FR-015's "cannot be opened/read")? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [x] CHK003 Is behavior specified for the same TCGplayer order identifier appearing twice within one packing-slip batch, as opposed to across two separate import operations (FR-008 only addresses the latter)? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK004 Are requirements defined for an upper bound on quantity values, or is any positive whole number accepted regardless of magnitude? [Gap, Spec §FR-003, FR-005]
- [x] CHK005 Are file-size or page-count limits specified for a single packing-slip PDF, independent of the ~200-order scale assumption? [Gap, Spec Assumptions]
- [x] CHK006 Is a retention/deletion policy specified for `ImportAttempt`/`ImportOrderResult` records over time, or is indefinite accumulation implicitly assumed? [Gap, Spec §FR-012]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Is "cannot be read with confidence" (FR-005) given any criteria beyond "the field is present," or does it rely entirely on implementation judgment for what counts as low-confidence? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK008 Is "practical at this scale" for synchronous processing (SC-006, Assumptions) bounded by any specific duration/timeout, or is it left entirely subjective? [Clarity, Spec §SC-006]
- [x] CHK009 Is "byte-for-byte identical" (SC-008) realistic given the source is extracted PDF text rather than a literal byte copy of the source field — could library-level whitespace/encoding normalization make this criterion unverifiable as literally written? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §SC-008, FR-017] — Resolved via `/speckit-analyze` (finding A1): SC-008 reworded to measure fidelity against the parser's own extracted text rather than the source PDF directly.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK010 Are the failure-type codes enumerated in FR-006 and the failure-code references in the `Import Attempt`/`Import Order Result` entity descriptions kept in a single source of truth, or could the two lists drift if one is edited without the other? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, Key Entities]
- [x] CHK011 Is the "Ready" order status (Assumptions) the only status this feature ever assigns, and is that consistent with there being no other status value defined or reserved anywhere in this spec? [Consistency, Spec Assumptions]
- [x] CHK012 Are the required-field lists in FR-005's prose and FR-005's implied validation (each required field individually named) consistent with the full field list in FR-002's extraction requirement? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, FR-005]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK013 Can SC-003 ("an operator can determine whether it succeeded or failed... without inspecting application code, database contents, or logs directly") be objectively verified today, given this feature explicitly has no consumer-facing interface yet? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK014 Are SC-007's concurrency guarantee and SC-009's disambiguation/preservation guarantee each verifiable by a single, unambiguous test, or do they bundle more than one testable claim per criterion? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007, SC-009]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK015 Are recovery/retry requirements defined for an operator who wants to correct and re-supply a rejected order's data (beyond "it was rejected, try again"), or is re-import the only documented path? [Gap, Coverage]
- [x] CHK016 Are non-English card/set names or non-ASCII characters in the source description addressed by any requirement, or left unstated? [Gap, Coverage]
- [x] CHK017 Are the primary (valid import), alternate (partial import), and exception (full rejection) scenario classes all represented with acceptance scenarios, and is a "recovery" class (e.g., re-import after a fix) intentionally out of scope or simply unaddressed? [Coverage, Spec §User Scenarios]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK018 Is behavior specified when the batch summary/index page itself is absent from an otherwise-valid multi-order file (as opposed to present-but-mismatched, which FR-013 covers)? [Gap, Spec §FR-013]
- [x] CHK019 Is behavior specified for a product-line description that matches more than one condition-prefix candidate, or where the condition segment is ambiguous between two of the fixed condition values referenced in FR-018/research.md? [Gap, Spec §FR-018]
- [x] CHK020 Is behavior specified for an Order Line whose quantity is a valid positive whole number but implausibly large for a real order (e.g., a likely parsing error rather than a real request)? [Gap, Edge Case]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK021 Are observability/monitoring requirements specified beyond the queryable `ImportAttempt`/`ImportOrderResult` records (e.g., is external alerting on repeated `UnreadablePdf` attempts in scope)? [Gap]
- [x] CHK022 Are requirements defined for what happens if the underlying database is unavailable mid-import (distinct from a validation-driven rejection), or is that left entirely to technical planning? [Gap, Spec §FR-016]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK023 Is the assumption that a future "caller" (import UI feature) will consume `IPackingSlipImportService` validated, or could this feature ship with no consumer, leaving FR-014's progress-exposure requirement unused in practice? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions, FR-014]
- [x] CHK024 Is the assumption of a small, fixed, enumerable TCGplayer condition-value vocabulary (underlying FR-018) validated against more than the one real example file reviewed during clarification? [Assumption, Spec §FR-018, Clarifications]
- [x] CHK025 Is the One Piece Card Game packing-slip format assumed to match the Pokémon/Magic/Lorcana format validated, or genuinely unconfirmed per PRD §31/§41? [Assumption, Spec §FR-002]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK026 Could FR-009's "no customer shipping information in any form" and FR-017's "retain the complete raw product description text... unmodified" ever conflict, if a product description field could in principle contain buyer-identifying text (e.g., a customized/personalized product line)? [Conflict-check, Spec §FR-009, FR-017]
- [x] CHK027 Is there a documented resolution for what "the entire import attempt" means for FR-006's failure-code surface when only some orders in a batch are affected by a `SummaryMismatch` — does the whole attempt fail, or only the mismatched orders? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006, FR-013]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify` — this file is independent of it
- Add comments or findings inline
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
